name: Shay

colleagues_competitors.name: Erin Claire Jones
colleagues_competitors.note: Human Design educator, author of How Do You Choose?

colleagues_competitors.name: Kathleen Cameron
colleagues_competitors.note: Manifestation/money-mindset content ("Is Manifestation a HOAX?", "MANIFEST MILLIONS"). Pattern: big-claim headline + self-aware skepticism bait to disarm doubt, then a huge outcome word. Beatable because it stays abstract — no Tuesday, no bank account, no kid named.

colleagues_competitors.name: Jamie Sea
colleagues_competitors.note: "The secret to making your business THRIVE," nervous-system mechanism reveals delivered as an insider secret. Beatable because her mechanism talk stays in the body/feelings register and rarely lands on a concrete business action — Shay's voice can do both: name the feeling AND the next step.

colleagues_competitors.name: Natalie Ellis / Bossbabe
colleagues_competitors.note: Founder-story vulnerability ("My Biggest Business Regret, A Million Dollar Mistake"). Beatable because it's vulnerability about herself, not about the buyer — Shay's edge is confessing what she SEES happening to the client, landing closer to "how is she in my head."

colleagues_competitors.name: Judith Manriquez
colleagues_competitors.note: Closest overlap. Soft reframes, gentle spiritual-affirmation headlines ("I wasn't failing. I was developing."). Beatable because it's soothing, not confrontational — Shay's sharper, funnier, more direct voice owns the confrontational edge in this exact zone, uncontested.

competitor_takeaway: Every one of them stays either abstract-aspirational (Kathleen, Bossbabe) or soft-soothing (Judith, Jamie Sea's gentler moments). None combine a confrontational, specific, funny voice with real execution proof — that's genuinely unclaimed territory.
